classification.difficultyReason: Direct integration of sine and cosine, including a region below the x-axis.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the area of the shaded region between $y=\sin x$ and the $x$-axis from $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$ to $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$.

spec.description: Sine graph with source shading from pi/6 to pi/2; this conflicts with the printed upper bound pi.
spec.mathematics: y=sin(x); shaded region pi/6 <= x <= pi/2, 0 <= y <= sin(x).

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the area of the shaded region between $y=\cos x$ and the $x$-axis from $x=\frac{2\pi}{3}$ to $x=\pi$.

spec.description: Cosine graph with source shading from 2pi/3 to pi; this conflicts with the printed lower bound pi/2.
spec.mathematics: y=cos(x); shaded region 2pi/3 <= x <= pi, cos(x) <= y <= 0.

answer.worked:
The curve is below the $x$-axis on this interval.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=-\int_{2\pi/3}^{\pi}\cos x\,dx\\&=-[\sin x]_{2\pi/3}^{\pi}\\&=-\left(0-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\&=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\text{ units}^2.\end{aligned}$$
